docs.title: serial-scale-hx711
docs.text:
Python driver for Arduino+HX711 serial weighing scales.

See the README for installation and usage.

docs.title: serial_scale_hx711.scale.Scale
docs.text:
Bases: SerialConnection

Arduino+HX711 serial weighing scale driver.

Sends single-character commands over serial and parses newline-terminated float responses from the firmware. Always call start() before reading; call disconnect() (or use as a context managed resource) when done.

docs.title: identify()
docs.text:
Send the identity command and return True if the firmware responds correctly.

The firmware replies with the string <SerialWeighingScale> once initialisation is complete. Returns False for any other response.

docs.title: read_weight()
docs.text:
Request a single weight reading from the firmware.

Returns:

Type Description float | None

Weight in grams rounded to two decimal places, or None if the

float | None

firmware response could not be parsed as a float.

docs.title: read_weight_blocking(n_valid=3, inter_read_delay=0.2, timeout=30)
docs.text:
Block until n_valid successful weight readings are collected, return their median.

Use this at every point in the calibration where the task must not proceed until the scale has returned a trustworthy value. Raises TimeoutError if the scale does not produce enough valid readings within timeout seconds.

docs.title: read_weight_repeated(n_readings=5, inter_read_delay=0.1)

docs.title: start(timeout=10)
docs.text:
Connect and wait for the scale firmware to finish initialising.

Firmware only responds to (identify) once the HX711 tare is complete, so polling identify() is sufficient; no need to hammer read_weight().

docs.title: tare()
docs.text:
Zero the scale and wait for the tare to propagate through the firmware buffer.

The firmware's LoadCell.tare() call is blocking (~100 ms). An additional 400 ms sleep ensures the rolling-average buffer is flushed before the next read_weight call.

docs.title: serial_scale_hx711.connect_serial_scale(serial_port_list=DEFAULT_TEST_PORTS)
docs.text: Connect to the first available serial scale from the provided list of ports.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install serial-scale-hx711

Python 3.10 or later is required. The only runtime dependency is pyserial.

docs.title: Hardware setup
docs.text:
You need three components:

Component Example part Arduino Uno any USB-serial Arduino HX711 amplifier SparkFun SEN-13879 Load cell SparkFun SEN-14727 (100 g) or SEN-14728 (500 g)

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text:
Connect the HX711 to the Arduino using the pin assignments hard-coded in the firmware:

HX711 pin Arduino pin DOUT Digital 2 SCK Digital 3 VCC 5 V GND GND

Connect the load cell to the HX711 following the colour-coding printed on the amplifier breakout board (typically: red = E+, black = E-, white = A-, green = A+).

docs.title: Firmware
docs.text: Flash scale_firmware/scale_firmware.ino to the Arduino using the Arduino IDE. The sketch depends on the HX711_ADC library (install via the Arduino Library Manager). After flashing, the scale communicates at 115200 baud and identifies itself as <SerialWeighingScale>.

docs.title: First reading
docs.text:
Plug the Arduino in via USB. Find its port (e.g. /dev/ttyACM0 on Linux, COM3 on Windows) then run:

from serial_scale_hx711 import Scale

scale = Scale(serial_port="/dev/ttyACM0")
scale.start()          # open port and wait for firmware to finish taring
print(scale.read_weight())  # prints weight in grams
scale.disconnect()

start() polls the firmware until the HX711 tare is complete (up to 10 s by default). If you do not know which port to use, see Usage - auto-detecting the port.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Part Example Notes Arduino Uno Any Uno-compatible board USB-A to USB-B cable for host connection HX711 amplifier SparkFun SEN-13879 24-bit ADC; 10 Hz or 80 Hz sample rate Load cell 100 g SparkFun SEN-14727 For small-rodent water rewards Load cell 500 g SparkFun SEN-14728 For heavier payloads or food hopper

docs.title: Firmware
docs.text: Flash the Arduino with the firmware from scale_firmware/ in this repository. The firmware uses olkal/HX711_ADC and reports weight over serial at 115200 baud. The scale identifies itself as <SerialWeighingScale> when first connected; the driver waits for this string during Scale.start().

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text:
Connect the HX711 board to the Arduino and wire the load cell to the HX711:

Load cell   HX711
----------  ------
Red (E+)    E+
Black (E-)  E-
White (A-)  A-
Green (A+)  A+

HX711       Arduino Uno
----------  -----------
VCC         3.3 V (or 5 V for HX711 modules with built-in regulator)
GND         GND
DT          pin 4
SCK         pin 5

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
The calibration factor is stored in Arduino EEPROM and loaded on boot. To recalibrate:

  1. Connect the scale and run Scale.start().
  2. Place a known weight on the load cell.
  3. Send the calibration command via serial or use the firmware's interactive prompt.
  4. The new factor is saved to EEPROM automatically.

The Scale.get_calibration_factor() method reads the current stored value.

docs.title: Basic connection
docs.text:
from serial_scale_hx711 import Scale

scale = Scale(serial_port="/dev/ttyACM0")
scale.start()   # open port and wait for firmware initialisation

Always call start() before reading. It blocks until the firmware has finished its power-on tare (up to timeout seconds, default 10).

docs.title: Auto-detecting the port
docs.text:
connect_serial_scale tries each port in order and returns the first one that responds correctly:

from serial_scale_hx711 import connect_serial_scale

scale = connect_serial_scale(["/dev/ttyACM0", "/dev/ttyACM1", "/dev/ttyACM2"])
if scale is None:
    raise RuntimeError("No scale found")

The default port list (DEFAULT_TEST_PORTS) covers /dev/ttyACM0 through /dev/ttyACM4.

docs.title: Taring
docs.text:
Remove all weight from the platform, then call tare() to zero the scale:

scale.tare()

tare() waits 500 ms after sending the command so that the firmware rolling-average buffer fully flushes before the next read.

docs.title: Single reading
docs.text:
weight = scale.read_weight()   # float (grams) or None on parse error

A return value of None means the firmware sent an unparseable response; check the serial connection and try again.

docs.title: Stable / averaged readings
docs.text: For a more reliable measurement, use one of the higher-level helpers.

docs.title: Fixed number of reads with statistical reduction
docs.text:
weight = scale.read_weight_reliable(n_readings=10, inter_read_delay=0.05)
# default measure is statistics.median; pass any callable
import statistics
weight = scale.read_weight_reliable(n_readings=10, measure=statistics.mean)

docs.title: Blocking until N valid reads are collected
docs.text:
Use this when you need to be sure the measurement is trustworthy before proceeding, for example in an automated calibration workflow:

weight = scale.read_weight_blocking(n_valid=5, timeout=30)

read_weight_blocking collects reads until n_valid non-None values have been received, then returns their median. It raises TimeoutError if that does not happen within timeout seconds.

docs.title: Collecting raw repeated reads
docs.text:
readings = scale.read_weight_repeated(n_readings=10, inter_read_delay=0.1)
# returns a list of valid (non-None) floats

docs.title: Continuous reading loop
docs.text:
import time

scale.tare()
try:
    while True:
        w = scale.read_weight()
        if w is not None:
            print(f"{w:.2f} g")
        time.sleep(0.1)
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    pass
finally:
    scale.disconnect()

docs.title: Reading the calibration factor
docs.text:
The firmware stores a fixed calibration factor compiled into the sketch. You can read it back at runtime for logging or diagnostics:

factor = scale.get_calibration_factor()
print(f"Calibration factor: {factor}")

To change the calibration factor you need to edit CALIBRATION_FACTOR in scale_firmware/scale_firmware.ino and re-flash the Arduino.

docs.title: Disconnecting
docs.text:
scale.disconnect()

disconnect() is also called automatically when the Scale object is garbage-collected, but calling it explicitly is recommended.
